Supersedes #36173 and addresses its final review findings.

## Motivation

SGLang normally computes the top-p cutoff from the original probability distribution and intersects that support with top-k. Some sampling paths instead applied top-k, renormalized the remaining probabilities, and then applied top-p. That applies top-p to whatever probability mass happens to remain after top-k, making its effect unpredictable and inconsistent with other sampling paths using the same parameters.

The affected paths are the FlashInfer min-p path, the shared EAGLE-family/standalone/n-gram verifier, and the target-distribution builder shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO. UNO's separate compact top-k path also needed the same fix; its behavior could otherwise depend on other requests in the batch.

## Modifications

- Apply top-p before top-k in the FlashInfer min-p path.
- Apply the same ordering in the shared EAGLE-family, standalone, and n-gram verifier.
- Correct dense/sparse target distributions shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO.
- Preserve the sparse top-k path by translating the top-p cutoff into the renormalized top-k distribution using the top-k support's original probability mass.
- Apply the same correction to UNO's separate compact top-k path.
- Fuse CUDA unseeded top-p rescaling by reusing the retained top-k maximum, avoiding a full-vocabulary maximum reduction and exponential intermediate.
- Preserve logsumexp for seeded/non-CUDA callers; UNO rejects deterministic inference.
- Document that fused FP32 rounding can change cutoff membership, without promising bitwise identity or trainer alignment.
- Reject `min_p > 0` for built-in speculative decoding, where it is not currently applied.
- Add focused CUDA regression tests for each corrected implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

The regressions use probabilities `[0.35, 0.25, 0.20, 0.05, 0.03, ...]`, `top_k=4`, and `top_p=0.82`. The FlashInfer min-p case also uses `min_p=0.1`.

The original top-p nucleus includes token 3 because the probability mass before it is `0.80`. Applying and renormalizing top-k first changes that mass to `0.80 / 0.85`, causing token 3 to be incorrectly removed.

Validated rebased commit `50e6ca6b73cc49214b5e9e28068b187ac3d7de2f` on an NVIDIA H200 with Python 3.12.3, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.18, and Triton 3.7.1.

`TestSamplingMaskCapture` and `test_speculative_sampling.py`: **18 passed, 6 subtests passed**, no failures/errors/skips.

Each regression passed with the fix and failed with pre-fix filtering:

| Path | With fix | Before fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FlashInfer min-p | Pass | Support length 3 instead of 4 |
| EAGLE, using the production FlashInfer kernels | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| Shared target builder, dense | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| Shared target builder, sparse | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| UNO compact | Pass | Compact support probability mismatch |

The same tests exercised pre-fix filtering from public base `d2a436446cca3d955358e7b4a5bf6881ea8591cd`; EAGLE retained the extracted helper signature for testability.

Ruff 0.15.1, isort 7.0.0, syntax, whitespace, and registry checks passed. The H200 results above apply to `50e6ca6b73cc49214b5e9e28068b187ac3d7de2f`, not current-head CI.

[Base CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39500026515) passed at `f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03`; Extra/AMD had failures. CI States below tracks newer runs.

<!-- lint: profile=evidence-heavy -->

### Historical HTTP validation at `f0c0a64`

All 10 HTTP checks passed at `f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03` on H200 using `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` revision `7ae557604adf67be50417f59c2c2f167def9a775`, Transformers 5.19.0, and the runtime below.

NGRAM accepted `min_p=0`. With `min_p=0.1`, non-streaming requests returned HTTP 400; streaming requests emitted `abort`, embedded status 400, and `[DONE]`. Each rejection mode ran twice; all four following valid requests succeeded. Ordinary sampling accepted `min_p=0.1`. Both servers remained healthy before teardown. Other speculative modes and PD deployment were not exercised. Source Rust extensions used `SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE=auto`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

These measurements predate fusion in `b94a95d5e805e0ee214c6d355a3a6cc79dd5e073`; see the [fused-helper validation summary](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41916#issuecomment-6328764169) for results and limitations.

Historical head `f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03` versus base `f0b65907227480afc376a66db62931b7e9c46c38`:

| Setup | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware/runtime | H200; driver 595.71.05; Python 3.12.15; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130; FlashInfer 0.7.2; Triton 3.8.0 |
| Functions | Production head functions and exact base definitions with unchanged dependencies; UNO retains `torch.compile(dynamic=True)` |
| Inputs | Seed 41916; FP32 normal logits, std=2; temperature=0.8; top-k=50; top-p=0.9; draft width=6 |
| Timing | Median microseconds/call; five alternating base/head samples; 200 CUDA Graph replays/sample; compilation and warmup excluded |
| Shape order | Vocabulary 32,768 then 128,256; batch 1, 16, 64 for each |

Outputs were finite and normalized; base/head sampling semantics intentionally differ.

| Path | Batch | Vocabulary | Base (us) | Head (us) | Added (us) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DFlash sparse | 1 | 32,768 | 79.85 | 99.50 | 19.65 |
| UNO compact | 1 | 32,768 | 28.75 | 38.01 | 9.26 |
| DFlash sparse | 16 | 32,768 | 130.29 | 158.38 | 28.09 |

| DFlash sparse | 64 | 128,256 | 896.05 | 1211.86 | 315.81 |
| UNO compact | 64 | 128,256 | 163.58 | 369.16 | 205.58 |

With top-p disabled at batch=16, vocabulary=128,256, DFlash measured 300.17 -> 300.31 us; UNO measured 57.71 -> 56.90 us. Costs increased 17-38% for DFlash and 32-126% for UNO in this sweep. End-to-end serving throughput and latency remain unmeasured.

`torch.profiler` CPU/CUDA traces used ten graph replays and three ordinary calls, after warmup. At batch=64, vocabulary=128,256:

| Path | Additional full-vocabulary work | Profile attribution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DFlash sparse | Eager `logsumexp`: max, subtract, exp, sum, final normalization | 9 kernels, ~350 us; ~188 MiB temporary tensor. Total kernel count: 30 -> 52. Unprofiled rerun: 886 -> 1199 us. |
| UNO compact | Compiled full-vocabulary max and exp-sum reductions | 4 kernels, ~206 us; two scans dominate. Total kernel count: 6 -> 10. Unprofiled rerun: 163 -> 369 us. |

DFlash's top-p kernel fell from ~53 to 5 us; kernel durations attribute costs but do not replace unprofiled timings.

UNO depends on shape warmup order. Starting with vocabulary=128,256 and batch 1 then 64 generated a single full-vocabulary reduction kernel (~113 us), with unprofiled timings 161 -> 275 us. Repeating the sweep restored 163 -> 369 us; the percentage is not universal.

import ast
import gc
import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import statistics
import subprocess
import time
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch

from sglang.srt.speculative import dflash_utils as dflash
from sglang.srt.speculative import uno_utils as uno

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = ROOT / 'benchmark-results.json'


def source_node(path, name):
    source = Path(path).read_text()
    node = next(n for n in ast.parse(source).body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == name)
    return source, node


def load_base(path, names, module):
    namespace = dict(vars(module))
    source = Path(path).read_text()
    nodes = [n for n in ast.parse(source).body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name in names]
    assert len(nodes) == len(names)
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=nodes, type_ignores=[]), str(path), 'exec'), namespace)
    return namespace


def capture(fn):
    # Compilation and allocator warmup are outside the measured region.
    for _ in range(4):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        output = fn()
    for _ in range(10):
        graph.replay()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    tensors = output if isinstance(output, tuple) else (output,)
    assert all(torch.isfinite(t).all().item() for t in tensors)
    probs = tensors[-1]
    assert torch.allclose(probs.sum(-1), torch.ones_like(probs.sum(-1)), atol=2e-5, rtol=2e-5)
    return graph, output


def measure(graph, repetitions=200):
    start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    start.record()
    for _ in range(repetitions):
        graph.replay()
    end.record()
    end.synchronize()
    return start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / repetitions

    for helper in ('_dflash_top_p_renorm_prob', '_dflash_top_k_renorm_prob'):
        _, before = source_node(ROOT / 'base_dflash_utils.py', helper)
        _, after = source_node(dflash.__file__, helper)
        assert ast.dump(before) == ast.dump(after), f'Dependency changed: {helper}'
    metadata = {
        'head': 'f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03',
        'base': 'f0b65907227480afc376a66db62931b7e9c46c38',
        'torch': torch.__version__, 'cuda': torch.version.cuda,
        'gpu': torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
        'driver': subprocess.check_output(['nvidia-smi', '--query-gpu=driver_version', '--format=csv,noheader'], text=True).strip(),
        'packages': {p: importlib.metadata.version(p) for p in ('flashinfer-python', 'triton', 'transformers')},
        'method': 'Production head functions, exact base function ASTs with unchanged production dependencies; UNO torch.compile(dynamic=True) retained. CUDA Graph replay, warmup and compilation excluded, 5 paired samples alternating order, 200 replays/sample. Synthetic fixed-seed float32 logits, std=2; temperature=.8; top_k=50; draft_width=6.',
        'scope': 'Sampling function microbenchmark only. No model inference or end-to-end latency claim. Base/head intentionally implement different distributions.',
        'source_sha256': {str(p.name): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in (ROOT/'base_dflash_utils.py', ROOT/'base_uno_utils.py', Path(dflash.__file__), Path(uno.__file__), Path(__file__))},
    }
    results = []
    cases = [(b, v, True) for v in (32768, 128256) for b in (1, 16, 64)] + [(16, 128256, False)]
    for bs, vocab, enabled in cases:
        torch.manual_seed(41916)
        width, k = 6, 50
        logits = torch.randn(bs * width, vocab, device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32) * 2
        temperatures = torch.full((bs, 1), .8, device='cuda')
        top_ks = torch.full((bs,), k, device='cuda', dtype=torch.int32)
        top_ps = torch.full((bs,), .9 if enabled else 1.0, device='cuda')
        info = SimpleNamespace(temperatures=temperatures, top_ks=top_ks, top_ps=top_ps, need_top_k_sampling=True, need_top_p_sampling=enabled)
        for path in ('dflash_sparse', 'uno_compact'):
            print(json.dumps({'starting': path, 'batch': bs, 'vocab': vocab, 'top_p_enabled': enabled}), flush=True)
            if path == 'dflash_sparse':
                args = dict(next_token_logits=logits, sampling_info=info, draft_token_num=width, bs=bs, max_top_k=k, uniform_top_k_value=k, use_sparse_topk=True)
                before = lambda: base_dflash['build_speculative_verify_target_probs'](**args)

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import psutil
import requests

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
BASE_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:31916'
RESULT = {'head': 'f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03', 'model': json.loads((ROOT/'model.json').read_text()), 'checks': [], 'launches': []}


def save():
    (ROOT/'http-results.json').write_text(json.dumps(RESULT, indent=2)+'\n')


def request(min_p, stream, expected_rejection, label):
    payload = {'text': 'The capital of France is', 'sampling_params': {'temperature': .7, 'top_k': 50, 'top_p': .9, 'min_p': min_p, 'max_new_tokens': 8}, 'stream': stream}
    start = time.monotonic()
    response = requests.post(BASE_URL+'/generate', json=payload, timeout=(10, 60))
    duration = time.monotonic()-start
    body = response.text
    if expected_rejection:
        assert 'min_p is not supported with NGRAM speculative decoding' in body, (response.status_code, body)
        assert response.status_code in (200, 400, 422), response.status_code
        if stream:
            assert 'data:' in body or response.status_code != 200, body
    else:
        assert response.status_code == 200, (response.status_code, body)
        parsed = response.json()
        assert isinstance(parsed.get('text'), str), parsed
        assert parsed['meta_info']['completion_tokens'] > 0, parsed
        assert parsed['meta_info']['finish_reason']['type'] != 'abort', parsed
    RESULT['checks'].append({'label': label, 'request': payload, 'status_code': response.status_code, 'elapsed_seconds': duration, 'response': body, 'passed': True})
    save()
    print(json.dumps({'label':label, 'status':response.status_code, 'seconds':duration, 'passed':True}), flush=True)


def stop_server(process):
    try:
        children = psutil.Process(process.pid).children(recursive=True)
    except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
        children = []
    try:
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
    except ProcessLookupError:
        pass
    try:
        process.wait(timeout=45)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        process.wait(timeout=15)
    for child in children:
        try:
            if child.is_running(): child.terminate()
        except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
            pass
    _, alive = psutil.wait_procs(children, timeout=15)
    for child in alive:
        try: child.kill()
        except psutil.NoSuchProcess: pass
    _, alive = psutil.wait_procs(alive, timeout=15)
    assert not [p.pid for p in alive if p.status() != psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE], 'server children survived'


def run_server(speculative):
    label = 'ngram' if speculative else 'ordinary'
    cmd = [sys.executable, '-m', 'sglang.launch_server', '--model-path', str(ROOT/'model'), '--host', '127.0.0.1', '--port', '31916', '--attention-backend', 'flashinfer', '--dtype', 'bfloat16', '--mem-fraction-static', '.5', '--max-running-requests', '8', '--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode', '8', '--context-length', '2048']
    if speculative:
        cmd += ['--speculative-algorithm', 'NGRAM', '--speculative-num-draft-tokens', '16']
    env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=str(ROOT/'source/python'), HF_HOME=str(ROOT/'hf'), HF_HUB_CACHE=str(ROOT/'hf/hub'), TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=str(ROOT/'inductor'), TRITON_CACHE_DIR=str(ROOT/'triton'), SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE='0', SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE='auto', SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=str(ROOT/'sglang-cache'))
    with open(ROOT/f'server-{label}.log', 'w') as log:
        process = subprocess.Popen(cmd, env=env, cwd=ROOT/'source', stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)
        RESULT['launches'].append({'mode':label, 'command':cmd, 'pid':process.pid})
        save()
        try:
            deadline = time.monotonic()+600
            while time.monotonic()<deadline:
                if process.poll() is not None:
                    raise RuntimeError(f'{label} server exited: {process.returncode}; see server-{label}.log')
                try:
                    if requests.get(BASE_URL+'/health',timeout=2).status_code == 200:
                        break
                except requests.RequestException:
                    pass
                time.sleep(2)
            else:
                raise TimeoutError(f'{label} server startup exceeded 600 seconds')
            print(f'SERVER_READY {label}',flush=True)
            if speculative:
                request(0, False, False, 'ngram valid initial control')
                for iteration in range(2):
                    for stream in (False, True):
                        request(.1, stream, True, f'ngram reject min_p=.1 stream={stream} repeat={iteration}')
                        request(0, False, False, f'ngram valid after rejection stream={stream} repeat={iteration}')
            else:
                request(.1, False, False, 'ordinary accepts min_p=.1')
            assert requests.get(BASE_URL+'/health',timeout=10).status_code == 200
            assert process.poll() is None
        finally:
            stop_server(process)
            RESULT['launches'][-1]['stopped'] = True
            save()


try:
    run_server(True)
    run_server(False)
    RESULT['complete'] = True
    print('HTTP_CHECK_COMPLETE',flush=True)
except Exception as exc:
    RESULT['error'] = repr(exc)
    raise
finally:
    save()

detail.body:
Supersedes #36173 and addresses its final review findings.

## Motivation

SGLang normally computes the top-p cutoff from the original probability distribution and intersects that support with top-k. Some sampling paths instead applied top-k, renormalized the remaining probabilities, and then applied top-p. That applies top-p to whatever probability mass happens to remain after top-k, making its effect unpredictable and inconsistent with other sampling paths using the same parameters.

The affected paths are the FlashInfer min-p path, the shared EAGLE-family/standalone/n-gram verifier, and the target-distribution builder shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO. UNO's separate compact top-k path also needed the same fix; its behavior could otherwise depend on other requests in the batch.

## Modifications

- Apply top-p before top-k in the FlashInfer min-p path.
- Apply the same ordering in the shared EAGLE-family, standalone, and n-gram verifier.
- Correct dense/sparse target distributions shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO.
- Preserve the sparse top-k path by translating the top-p cutoff into the renormalized top-k distribution using the top-k support's original probability mass.
- Apply the same correction to UNO's separate compact top-k path.
- Fuse CUDA unseeded top-p rescaling by reusing the retained top-k maximum, avoiding a full-vocabulary maximum reduction and exponential intermediate.
- Preserve logsumexp for seeded/non-CUDA callers; UNO rejects deterministic inference.
- Document that fused FP32 rounding can change cutoff membership, without promising bitwise identity or trainer alignment.
- Reject `min_p > 0` for built-in speculative decoding, where it is not currently applied.
- Add focused CUDA regression tests for each corrected implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

The regressions use probabilities `[0.35, 0.25, 0.20, 0.05, 0.03, ...]`, `top_k=4`, and `top_p=0.82`. The FlashInfer min-p case also uses `min_p=0.1`.

The original top-p nucleus includes token 3 because the probability mass before it is `0.80`. Applying and renormalizing top-k first changes that mass to `0.80 / 0.85`, causing token 3 to be incorrectly removed.

Validated rebased commit `50e6ca6b73cc49214b5e9e28068b187ac3d7de2f` on an NVIDIA H200 with Python 3.12.3, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.18, and Triton 3.7.1.

`TestSamplingMaskCapture` and `test_speculative_sampling.py`: **18 passed, 6 subtests passed**, no failures/errors/skips.

Each regression passed with the fix and failed with pre-fix filtering:

| Path | With fix | Before fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FlashInfer min-p | Pass | Support length 3 instead of 4 |
| EAGLE, using the production FlashInfer kernels | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| Shared target builder, dense | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| Shared target builder, sparse | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| UNO compact | Pass | Compact support probability mismatch |

The same tests exercised pre-fix filtering from public base `d2a436446cca3d955358e7b4a5bf6881ea8591cd`; EAGLE retained the extracted helper signature for testability.

Ruff 0.15.1, isort 7.0.0, syntax, whitespace, and registry checks passed. The H200 results above apply to `50e6ca6b73cc49214b5e9e28068b187ac3d7de2f`, not current-head CI.
